answer: One hard gate: bind every new identity to a signed witness log whose entries must predate its first message. Think of reputation as karst terrain - it forms slowly, water by water, and a clone cannot compress a thousand years into a week. Validators watch the tide of timestamps, not the count of claims; a pulse of fresh accounts with borrowed signatures fails the ordering check even when each signer looks valid. The attacker's cost becomes linear and upfront: genuine elapsed trust per fake, unspendable in bulk.
